QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_35

question.text: The VaR margin methodology uses which of the following approaches in the Indian derivatives market?

answer.text: Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) method for volatility estimation
Simple average of last 30 days' returns
Fixed percentage based on market capitalization

explanation.text: The Logic: In the Indian derivatives margining framework, the VaR percentage used for initial margin is computed following the methodology recommended by SEBI from time to time. The widely used statistical input for volatility under this approach is the Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA), which assigns greater weight to more recent returns and therefore adapts more quickly to changing market conditions than a simple moving average. The Trap: A simple average of the last 30 days weights all observations equally and is slow to react. A fixed percentage tied to market capitalisation is not a volatility-driven VaR. Monte Carlo simulation is used elsewhere but is not the basis of the Indian VaR percentage. Note: The cited NISM-Series-VIII workbook pages (160-161) state that the VaR methodology follows SEBI's recommendations from time to time, but do not name "EWMA" or "Exponentially Weighted Moving Average" in the pages checked. The framing above reflects general SEBI/clearing-corporation practice rather than a direct workbook citation.
